comment: The draft already recognises governed verification before formal action in public-health surveillance and override/accountability mechanisms in clinical decision support. Consider articulating a broader principle for consequential automated or rules-based determinations where underlying evidence is incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous or otherwise falls outside normal decision conditions.

citation.raw: §Appendix C — Public Health Surveillance Platform; see also Computable Decision Support Engine p.228; 188 l.PHSP 214–220; CDSE 138–140

public.text: The draft already recognises governed verification before formal action in public-health surveillance and override/accountability mechanisms in clinical decision support. Consider articulating a broader principle for consequential automated or rules-based determinations where underlying evidence is incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous or otherwise falls outside normal decision conditions.
public.suggestedRevision: Consider adding: “Where automated or rules-based determinations carry material consequences, countries should define proportionate exception and review mechanisms for situations in which evidence is incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous or otherwise falls outside normal decision conditions. Such mechanisms may include authorised review, reason capture, escalation and auditability, according to national law, policy and risk.”
